Question: \(A\) and \(B\) together can do a job in \(2\) days; \(B\) and \(C\) can do it in four days; and \(A\) and \(C\) in \(2\dfrac25\) days. The number of days required for \(A\) to do the job alone is:
Solution:
Work rates add when people work together, so convert the completion times into fractions of the job completed per day. Let \(a,b,c\) be the constant daily rates of \(A,B,C\), respectively, taking the whole job as \(1\). Since \(2\frac25=\frac{12}{5}\),
\[
a+b=\frac12,\qquad
b+c=\frac14,\qquad
a+c=\frac5{12}.
\]
To isolate \(A\)'s contribution, add the first and third equations and subtract the second. The contributions of \(B\) and \(C\) cancel:
\[
2a=(a+b)+(a+c)-(b+c)
=\frac12+\frac5{12}-\frac14
=\frac23.
\]
Thus \(a=\frac13\) job per day. Completing one job therefore takes \(1\div\frac13=\boxed{3}\) days, choice B.
